# Multiplexed receive messages generated by CoGeNT (BMS19_100 / BMS20_100)

Date: 2026-10-11. Design approved in chat on 2026-10-11 ("Approve (Recommended)").

## Goal

*Generate code* produces the complete code for enabled multiplexed receive messages whose layout the
legacy generator rejects (today BMS19_100 and BMS20_100), in the layout and with the receive logic of the
hand code in the S2XX workspace (`D:\networkgen\dc.app.scl.vehiclecomm`, read only). The output for every
other message, VCU5_500 included, stays byte-identical. *Re-apply edits* is no longer needed for these
messages.

## Context

- The legacy generator supports one multiplex layout (VCU5_500: every multiplexed signal starts at bit 0
  of the frame, multiplexor in byte 7). For any other enabled multiplexed message it stops with
  "multiplexed ... layout" (`msg.multiplex_layout_problem`, `msg.find_unsupported_multiplex`).
- BMS19_100 (8-bit multiplexor in byte 0, indexes 0..10, three 16-bit Intel temperatures per index from
  bit 16) and BMS20_100 (4-bit multiplexor in bits 0..3, indexes 0..15, six 10-bit Intel voltages per
  index from bit 4) are received by SMART_CORE. Their Rx enable is off in the configuration; their code
  was written by hand in the workspace and is carried to new DBC versions with *Re-apply edits*.
- The hand code was analysed section by section (2026-10-11). Message-level items (buffers, handles,
  receive table, VNIM enum/lists, resources, host tables) are exactly what the generator emits for any
  enabled receive message. Signal-level items follow fixed patterns described below. The analysis also
  found an overlap of data-changed flags and three copy-paste slips in the BMS20 code (section 9).

## Scope

In scope: receive (Rx) multiplexed application messages, classic CAN (DLC <= 8), one multiplexor
(`M`), multiplexed signals (`mN`) in Intel byte order with at most 32 bits, any number of indexes, plain
(non-multiplexed) signals besides the multiplexor allowed.

Not in scope (clear error, section 10): transmitted multiplexed messages, Motorola multiplexed signals,
multiplexed signals longer than 32 bits, extended multiplexing, CAN FD frames. VCU5_500-style messages keep
the legacy code path unchanged.

## Terms

- *Legacy-style message*: a multiplexed message that `multiplex_layout_problem` accepts (today VCU5_500).
  Generated exactly as before.
- *Indexed message*: an enabled multiplexed receive message that `multiplex_layout_problem` rejects and
  that is in scope. Generated with the rules of this document.
- *Fixed signals*: the multiplexor and any non-multiplexed signals of an indexed message.
- *Multiplexed signals*: the `mN` signals.
- *Signal order* of an indexed message: multiplexed signals sorted by (index, start bit), then the
  plain non-multiplexed signals by start bit, then the multiplexor.

## 1. Message types (nw_il_msg.h)

Placement: the types of indexed messages (sorted by message name) follow the types of the legacy-style
multiplexed messages and precede the regular message types of the same (Tx/Rx) section, where the hand
code puts them.

Each multiplexed signal is cut into byte-aligned bit fields named `<SIGNAL>_<k>` (k = 0, 1, ... in Intel
order), as the legacy generator does for multi-byte signals; a signal inside one byte keeps its name.
Bit fields are `CAN_UINT8 name:width;`. Gaps are `CAN_UINT8 unused<b>:width;` where `<b>` is the frame byte
in which the gap starts.

Two layouts, chosen automatically:

**Data union** - when the bytes touched by multiplexed signals (any index) and the bytes touched by fixed
signals are disjoint. Region = first..last byte touched by multiplexed signals.
- Per index `i` (0..max): `typedef struct { fields of index i, laid out from the region start, ending at
  the last byte that index uses } <MUX>_<i>_sigType;`
- `typedef union { CAN_UINT8 sig_buffer[<region bytes>]; <MUX>_<i>_sigType <mux>_<i>; ... }
  <GROUP>_Sigbuf;` with `<GROUP>` = multiplexor name without a trailing `_INDEX`, plus `_DATA`
  (BMS_CELLTEMP_INDEX gives BMS_CELLTEMP_DATA), `<mux>` = multiplexor name in lower case.
- `/* <MSG> */ typedef struct { fixed-signal and unused fields before the region; <GROUP>_Sigbuf
  <group>; fields after the region } <MSG>_msgType;`
- BMS19_100: byte 0 multiplexor, `unused1:8`, union of 6 bytes (indexes 0..9 use 6 bytes, index 10 uses 4).

**Frame union** - otherwise (a byte holds both a fixed and a multiplexed signal).
- Per index `i`: `typedef struct { the whole frame for index i: fixed signals, the signals of index i,
  unused gaps, up to the last used byte } <MUX>_<i>_sigType;`
- `/* <MSG> */ typedef union { CAN_UINT8 msgBuffer[<DLC>]; <MUX>_<i>_sigType <mux>_<i>; ... }
  <MSG>_msgType;`
- BMS20_100: every index struct starts with `BMS_CELLVOLTAGE_INDEX:4`.

The `<MSG>_buf` union, `Rx_buffer` member, extern declarations and everything else at message level stay
as generated for any message.

## 2. Signal access

- Data union: multiplexed signal of index i: `<MSG>.<msg>.<group>.<mux>_<i>.<FIELD>`; fixed signal:
  `<MSG>.<msg>.<FIELD>`.
- Frame union: multiplexed signal of index i: `<MSG>.<msg>.<mux>_<i>.<FIELD>`; fixed signal through index
  0: `<MSG>.<msg>.<mux>_0.<FIELD>`.
- The same paths with `Rx_buffer.<msg>` in `PreCopy`.
- C type of a signal: `CAN_UINT8` up to 8 bits, `CAN_UINT16` up to 16, `CAN_UINT32` up to 32.
- A signal that is one bit field gets put/get macros; a signal of several bit fields gets put/get
  functions (legacy rule). Values are assembled and split with the legacy patterns (shift by the widths of
  the lower fields, two-digit masks such as `0x0f`).

## 3. Receive logic (nw_il_par.c)

- Shadow variable per multiplexed signal, declared after the message buffers:
  `<C type> <MSG>_<rest>;` where `<rest>` is the signal name with the longest common prefix of message and
  signal name removed (BMS19_100 + BMS_CELLTEMP1 gives `BMS19_100__CELLTEMP1`).
- `<MSG>_PreCopy`: local `rValue` of the widest signal type; when not suspended:
  1. if the multiplexor differs between the message buffer and `Rx_buffer`, set the multiplexor's
     data-changed flag;
  2. for each index i: `if(Rx_buffer.<path of multiplexor> == i)` { for each signal of index i in start-bit
     order: assemble `rValue` from `Rx_buffer`; if it differs from the shadow, store it and set the
     signal's flag };
  3. plain non-multiplexed signals (if any): compare like the legacy `PreCopy`.
- Put/get functions read and write the message buffer (the current frame), like the hand code and like the
  legacy VCU5_500 code; the application reads them in the indication, after checking the index.
- `PreCopy` functions of indexed messages follow the last regular `PreCopy`; put and get functions follow
  the last regular ones (hand-code placement); within each block: messages by name, signals in signal order.

## 4. Data-changed flags and IL_MUX_MSG_OFFSET_ID (nw_il_par.h)

- Regular signals keep the legacy allocation; signals of indexed messages are left out of it, so every
  regular flag is unchanged. Let G be the number of flag bytes the regular signals use (the legacy
  `IL_NUM_OF_RX_DATA_CHANGED_FLAG`).
- Indexed messages get a separate area: bits allocated in order - for each indexed message (by name) its
  multiplexed and plain signals in signal order (without the multiplexor), then the multiplexors of all
  indexed messages (by message name). M = bytes of the area.
- `#define IL_NUM_OF_RX_DATA_CHANGED_FLAG   (G + M)` and `#define IL_MUX_MSG_OFFSET_ID   G`; macros use
  `il_Rx_DataChanged_Flag[IL_MUX_MSG_OFFSET_ID + k]`; the area's macros follow the last regular flag macros.
- Without indexed messages both lines stay as today (no `IL_MUX_MSG_OFFSET_ID`).
- G is computed, so the area can never overlap regular flags (40024: G = 162, 41490: G = 163).

## 5. Other nw_il_par.h items

- Put/get macros of one-field signals of indexed messages (per message by name: its one-field signals in
  signal order, the multiplexor last) follow the last regular put/get macros.
- Put/get function prototypes of indexed messages follow the last regular prototypes (same order as the
  functions).
- No `VNIM_RX_<signal>()` macros for signals of indexed messages (the hand code has none: the host
  receives the whole frame); likewise no `VNIM_IS_<signal>_MISSING()` in nw_vnim_app_signals_par.h
  (ruling made while planning).

## 6. VNIM (nw_vnim_app_signals_par.c)

All per-message code stays in the generator's sorted position and template; only the signal lists differ:
- error-healing `ILSet_..._DataChanged()` list and the per-message on-fail case: signal order (multiplexor
  last);
- the indication's check-and-clear list: the multiplexor first, then signal order without it (hand-code
  order);
- the representative signal of a message (timeout handler, IPCL case, on-fail case) is the last signal of
  the signal order = the multiplexor (as for VCU5_500);
- the on-fail initialisation list: the entries of indexed messages follow the last regular entry; per
  message (by name) the multiplexor first, then signal order without it.
- On-fail values come from the signal settings (TX/RX signals page) as for every signal; defaults from the
  DBC start value (cell temperatures 500 = 0x1F4). Found while implementing: the DBC parser ignored the start
  value of signals whose DBC name is not upper case (BMS_CellTemp1); it now matches names case-insensitively
  (only the signals page reads per-signal DBC attributes).
- The indication of an indexed message that uses the delayed notification (`<MSG>_msg_changed`) also
  notifies the host at once, as the hand code does: every frame carries another index and the 200 ms
  notification alone would drop frames (found while implementing).

## 7. Unchanged outputs

Handles, `IL_RX_NUM_*`, receive frame table, `vnim_msg_byte_position` / `vnim_msg_bit_mask`, node lists,
DTC/fault lists, resources, host-manager entries, receive rules and dispatch (`can_rxrule.cfg`,
`nw_can_dll.h`) are generated as for any enabled receive message. With BMS19_100/BMS20_100 enabled their
`additional_rx_messages` entries in the Receive FIFO settings are redundant (no duplicate rule is made).

## 8. Expected result against the workspace

Generating the 40024 configuration with BMS19_100 and BMS20_100 enabled reproduces the workspace's BMS code
(compared ignoring white space and blank lines) apart from section 9.

## 9. Intended differences from the hand code

1. `IL_MUX_MSG_OFFSET_ID` 162 instead of 161 (40024) and `(162 + 17)`: with 161, TCU6_CRC, TIME_TO_CHARGE,
   FOD_ALERT and RESERVED_WLC share flag bits 0x1..0x8 of byte 161 with BMS_CELLTEMP1..4.
2. `BMS20_100_PreCopy` sets the BMS_CELLVOLTAGE_INDEX flag (hand code: BMS_CELLTEMP_INDEX).
3. BMS20_100 on-fail case: `NM_MSG_MISSING(VNIM_BMS20_100_MSGID)` and the BMS_CELLVOLTAGE_INDEX flag (hand
   code: VNIM_BMS19_100_MSGID and BMS_CELLTEMP_INDEX); the multiplexor is set once (hand code: twice).
4. BMS20_100 signals are in the on-fail initialisation list (missing in the hand code).
5. `ILRxPut_BMS_CELLVOLTAGE26` / `32` store the upper 8 bits shifted by 2 (the signal starts at bit 14:
   2 + 8 bits); the hand code shifts by 3 (found while implementing).
6. (Removed at the user's request, 2026-10-11: indexed messages get no message-loss case, as in the hand
   code; they keep the message-gain case.)
7. The all-frames IPCL case (`ALL_RX_FRAME_IPCL_INDEX`) sets the BMS19_100 / BMS20_100 multiplexor flags, as
   for every other message (missing in the hand code; found while implementing).
8. `vnim_msg_byte_position` / `vnim_msg_bit_mask` have one entry per message (hand code: 192 for 193).
9. Formatting: the generator's spaces instead of the hand tabs; on-fail values in the generator's format
   (`0x0u`, hand code partly `0x00`); `~0x20u` in `ILClr_BMS_CELLVOLTAGE78_DataChanged` (hand code `~0x20`);
   the init values as the signals page writes the DBC start value (`0x1f4u`, hand code `0x1F4u`; type
   0x1F4 on the page to get the hand-code text).
`tests/test_mux_reference.py` pins exactly this list (counted, white space ignored) against the workspace.

## 10. Errors

`find_unsupported_multiplex` keeps stopping generation (same popup style, nothing written) for enabled
multiplexed messages that are neither legacy-style nor in scope, naming the message and the reason:
transmitted, Motorola multiplexed signal, multiplexed signal longer than 32 bits, more than one
multiplexor / extended multiplexing, DLC above 8, multiplexed signals but no multiplexor, or a
multiplexed signal overlapping a fixed signal.

## 11. GUI, Receive FIFO and reports

- TX/RX messages page: BMS19_100 / BMS20_100 can be enabled (no error); their 130 signals appear as new
  signals on the TX/RX signals page.
- `MANUAL_ACTIONS.md`: no "interaction-layer and VNIM code" action for an `additional_rx_messages` entry
  whose message is enabled (its code is generated); a REVIEW note says the entry is redundant.
- USER_GUIDE.md / Help, FIFO_MULTIPLEXING.md and HANDOFF.md describe multiplexed messages and the new rules;
  the error table entry for multiplexed messages is updated.

## 12. Testing

- Unit tests on a synthetic DBC (no workspace content): data-union and frame-union messages, a message
  with a plain signal, unused naming, access paths, flag area and offset, ordering, put/get/PreCopy text,
  every error of section 10.
- All existing golden and regression tests unchanged (VCU5_500 byte-identical).
- Reference test (runs only where the workspace exists, like `tests/test_reference_workspace.py`): the
  40024 fixture with BMS19_100/BMS20_100 enabled; every BMS line of the 11 files equals the workspace
  (white space ignored) except the exact list of section 9; every other line equals the plain generation.
- GUI test: enabling both messages and generating succeeds; packaged-exe smoke test.

## 13. Risks

- The legacy generators print while computing; hooks must not change their output for other messages -
  guarded by the golden tests.
- The hand code may contain a message-level item the generator adds or lacks; the reference test finds it,
  and it is handled under section 9.

## 14. Re-apply edits once the messages are generated (added 2026-10-11 on request)

Request: "make sure these hand edits won't ruin the generated code ... if the DBC doesn't have BMS19 or 20
no need to have them".

- A *hand-added message* is a receive message with a `VNIM_<MSG>_MESSAGE` handle in the edited
  `nw_il_par.h` but not in the previous generation (today BMS19_100, BMS20_100).
- New generation has the message (it is enabled and generated): its hand code is not re-applied - the
  generated code is kept. Edit regions that only concern such a message (its name, its signals, the
  multiplex flag area) are left out of the merge; `IL_RX_NUM_*` keeps the new value plus only the user's
  other changes (the message is not counted twice); `IL_MUX_MSG_OFFSET_ID` and
  `IL_NUM_OF_RX_DATA_CHANGED_FLAG` come from the new generation. Report: "now generated".
- The new DBC does not contain the message: its hand code is not re-applied. Report: "not in the DBC".
- The new DBC contains it but its Rx enable is off: re-applied as today; the report says that enabling it
  lets CoGeNT generate it.
- All other hand edits (NM transmit table, Tx overrides, Tx confirmation callbacks, REM order and macros,
  TC_NSM, CRANK_COUNT) are re-applied as today.
- Checks after the merge: no definition doubled or missing, no reference to a message without a handle,
  table sizes, handle order (existing checks), plus: every hand-added message is either generated, left
  out, or re-applied - never two copies.
- Test with the real case (local): previous generation `CODE_GEN\DBC_40024`, the workspace, new generation
  41490 with BMS19_100/BMS20_100 enabled: the result contains the generated BMS code once (section 9
  corrections included), all other hand edits, and passes every check. And 41490 with a DBC copy without
  BMS19_100/BMS20_100: no BMS code at all.
